name: The Seven Lighthouses
description: An original long journey along the Quiet Sea, 700 km from salt desert to northern ice, relighting seven lighthouses that went dark in one night. Comes with its own hand-drawn map.

salt-gate.name: The Salt Gate
salt-gate.text: Seven lights went dark in one night. The keepers' guild gives you the last ember and a map.

light-1.name: Dune Light
light-1.text: Sand to the windows. You clear the stairs and light the first lamp.

three-wells.name: Three Wells Oasis
three-wells.text: Palms, shade and cold water. A caravan heading north lets you walk beside it.

light-2.name: Cape of Winds Light
light-2.text: The wind nearly takes the ember. You shield it and the light flares.

shepherds-pass.name: Shepherds' Pass
shepherds-pass.text: From the top of the steppe highlands you can see the whole coast and three lights burning behind you.

light-3.name: Stone Sentinels Light
light-3.text: Standing stones ring the tower like old keepers.

rye-valley.name: Rye Valley Mills
rye-valley.text: Windmills turn over golden fields. The millers bake you bread for the road.

light-4.name: Wreck Light
light-4.text: A broken ship lies on the sand. Tonight no one else will join it.

misty-fens.name: The Misty Fens
misty-fens.text: Reeds higher than your head. You walk the old plank road, one board at a time.

light-5.name: Heron Light
light-5.text: Herons nest on the gallery and don't mind you at all.

birch-grove.name: The Birch Grove
birch-grove.text: White trunks and the first cold night. You sleep by a small fire.

light-6.name: Silent Light
light-6.text: Here even the sea is quiet. The lamp catches with a soft sound.

light-7.name: North Light
light-7.text: The last lamp takes the ember. Seven lights burn along the Quiet Sea, and above you the sky begins to glow.

story.heat: Heat shimmers over the salt. The ember in its lantern is the only thing cooler than the air.
story.caravan: The camel drivers sing to keep time. You learn the chorus by the second evening.
story.half: Halfway. Behind you, three lights. Ahead, four dark towers waiting.
story.fog: The fog is so thick you navigate by the smell of the sea.
story.snow: Snow squeaks under your boots. The North Light stands on the last cliff before the ice.

facts.pharos: The Pharos of Alexandria, one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World, gave its name to lighthouses in many languages: phare, faro, far.
facts.singing-dunes: Some dunes sing: when sand avalanches down their face, it can produce a low hum heard kilometres away.
facts.fresnel: In 1822 Augustin-Jean Fresnel designed a ringed lens that let a single lamp shine for tens of kilometres.
facts.steppe: The Eurasian Steppe runs for about 8000 km, from the Danube to Manchuria.
facts.carnac: At Carnac in Brittany more than 3000 prehistoric standing stones run in long rows across the fields.
facts.windmills: The earliest known windmills turned in Persia over a thousand years ago, with their sails on a vertical axis.
facts.characteristic: Every lighthouse has its own characteristic, a pattern of flashes, so sailors can tell one light from another at night.
facts.peat: Peatlands cover only about 3% of the land, yet store roughly twice as much carbon as all the world's forests.
facts.birch: Birches are pioneers: they are often the first trees to grow back after a fire or on bare ground.
facts.permafrost: In the tundra only a thin top layer thaws in summer; below lies permafrost that can stay frozen for thousands of years.
facts.aurora: Auroras glow when particles from the Sun hit the upper atmosphere; the common green light comes from oxygen about 100–300 km up.

highlands.name: Highlander
highlands.description: Cross the steppe highlands above 800 m.

big-day.name: Long Day's March
big-day.description: Walk 20 km in a single day.
